agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Analyze icons, importance, styles of entries in a directory."""
import sys, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/tools")
from run import run, show

ESC = re.compile(r"\x1b\[([0-9;]*)m")

def parse_line(line):
    # returns list of (style, text) segments
    segs = []
    cur = ""
    pos = 0
    for m in ESC.finditer(line):
        if m.start() > pos:
            segs.append((cur, line[pos:m.start()]))
        code = m.group(1)
        if code == "0":
            cur = ""
        else:
            cur = code
        pos = m.end()
    if pos < len(line):
        segs.append((cur, line[pos:]))
    return segs

def analyze(d, extra=()):
    results = {}
    for c in range(-5, 6):
        out = run(["/workspace/executable", "-I=%d" % c, "-c", "false", "-S", "false"] + list(extra), cwd=d)
        for line in out.split("\n"):
            if not line.strip(): continue
            segs = parse_line(line)
            # name is last segment(s); icon is first
            text = "".join(t for _, t in segs)
            # find name: strip trailing; the name segments are those after the icon area
            # The icon area: first 2 columns + 1 space
            # Simplest: name = text[3:] (icon + space + align), minus suffix
            name = text[3:]
            # style for name: style of last non-empty segment
            style = segs[-1][0]
            r = results.setdefault(name, {"icon": None, "styles": {}})
            iconseg = segs[0]
            r["icon"] = show(text[:3])
            r["styles"][c] = style
            r["icon_style"] = iconseg[0] if iconseg[1].strip() else ""
    for name, r in sorted(results.items()):
        # importance: cutoff where style has no 2/3/4
        imp = None
        for c in range(-5, 6):
            s = r["styles"].get(c)
            if s is None: continue
            codes = s.split(";") if s else []
            if not any(x in ("2","3","4") for x in codes):
                imp = c
                break
        base_style = r["styles"].get(imp, "") if imp is not None else "?"
        print("%-30s imp=%-3s icon=%-14s style=%-10s iconstyle=%s" % (name, imp, r["icon"], base_style, r.get("icon_style")))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    analyze(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ".", sys.argv[2:])

//! The configuration structures and the built-in defaults.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

	#[serde(default)]
	pub icons: BTreeMap<String, String>,

	pub specs: Vec<Spec>,

	pub entry_const: EntryConst,

}

/// A specification that applies to nodes whose name matches a pattern.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]

	#[serde(deserialize_with = "deserialize_regex")]
	pub pattern: Regex,
	#[serde(default)]
	pub icons: Vec<String>,
	#[serde(default)]
	pub style: Option<String>,
	#[serde(default)]
	pub importance: Option<i8>,
	#[serde(default)]
	pub collapse: Option<Collapse>,
}

fn deserialize_regex<'de, D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Regex, D::Error> {
	let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
	Regex::new(&s).map_err(de::Error::custom)
}

	pub symlink: BTreeMap<SymState, SymlinkInfo>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]

	#[serde(default)]

	}

	}

//! Command line interface.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use clap::builder::PossibleValuesParser;
use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use regex::Regex;

use crate::enums::{DetailField, SortField, Typ, UnitSystem};
use crate::utils::term::help_width;

/// The parsed and normalised command line arguments.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Args {
	pub paths: Vec<PathBuf>,
	pub details: Vec<DetailField>,
	pub header: bool,
	pub unit: UnitSystem,
	pub grid: bool,
	pub down: bool,
	pub icon: bool,
	pub suffix: bool,
	pub sym: bool,
	pub collapse: bool,
	pub align: bool,
	pub typs: Vec<Typ>,
	pub imp: i8,
	pub exclude: Option<Regex>,
	pub only: Option<Regex>,
	pub sort_bases: Vec<SortField>,
}

const ABOUT: &str = "pls is a prettier and powerful ls(1) for the pros.";
const LONG_ABOUT: &str = "pls is a prettier and powerful ls(1) for the pros.

Read docs: https://pls.cli.rs/
Get source: https://github.com/pls-rs/pls/
Sponsor: https://github.com/sponsors/dhruvkb/";

fn names<T>(values: &'static [(&'static str, T)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {
	values.iter().map(|(name, _)| *name).collect()
}

fn bool_arg(name: &'static str, short: char, long: &'static str, default: &'static str, help: &'static str) -> Arg {
	Arg::new(name)
		.short(short)
		.long(long)
		.value_name(name.to_uppercase())
		.help(help)
		.default_value(default)
		.value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(["true", "false"]))
}

fn parse_regex(s: &str) -> Result<Regex, regex::Error> {
	Regex::new(s)
}

/// Build the command line interface definition.
pub fn command() -> Command {
	Command::new("pls")
		.version("0.0.1-beta.9")
		.about(ABOUT)
		.long_about(LONG_ABOUT)
		.term_width(help_width())
		.arg(
			Arg::new("paths")
				.value_name("PATHS")
				.help("the paths to list, each of which may be a file or directory")
				.num_args(0..)
				.default_value(".")
				.value_parser(clap::value_parser!(PathBuf)),
		)
		.next_help_heading("Detail view")
		.arg(
			Arg::new("details")
				.short('d')
				.long("det")
				.value_name("DETAILS")
				.help("the data points to show about each node")
				.action(ArgAction::Append)
				.default_value("none")
				.value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(names(DetailField::CLI_VALUES))),
		)
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"header",
			'H',
			"header",
			"true",
			"show headers above columnar data",
		))
		.arg(
			Arg::new("unit")
				.short('u')
				.long("unit")
				.value_name("UNIT")
				.help("the type of units to use for the node sizes")
				.default_value("binary")
				.value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(names(UnitSystem::CLI_VALUES))),
		)
		.next_help_heading("Grid view")
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"grid",
			'g',
			"grid",
			"false",
			"display node names in multiple columns",
		))
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"down",
			'D',
			"down",
			"false",
			"display node names column-first",
		))
		.next_help_heading("Presentation")
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"icon",
			'i',
			"icon",
			"true",
			"display icons next to node names",
		))
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"suffix",
			'S',
			"suffix",
			"true",
			"display node type suffixes after the node name",
		))
		.arg(bool_arg("sym", 'l', "sym", "true", "show symlink targets"))
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"collapse",
			'c',
			"collapse",
			"true",
			"show dependent nodes as children of their principal nodes",
		))
		.arg(bool_arg(
			"align",
			'a',
			"align",
			"true",
			"align items accounting for leading dots",
		))
		.next_help_heading("Filtering")
		.arg(
			Arg::new("typs")
				.short('t')
				.long("typ")
				.value_name("TYPES")
				.help("the set of node types to include in the output")
				.action(ArgAction::Append)
				.default_value("all")
				.value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(names(Typ::CLI_VALUES))),
		)
		.arg(
			Arg::new("imp")
				.short('I')
				.long("imp")
				.value_name("IMP")
				.help("the importance cutoff to dim or hide unimportant files")
				.default_value("0")
				.value_parser(clap::value_parser!(i8)),
		)
		.arg(
			Arg::new("exclude")
				.short('e')
				.long("exclude")
				.value_name("EXCLUDE")
				.help("the pattern of files to selectively hide from the output")
				.value_parser(parse_regex),
		)
		.arg(
			Arg::new("only")
				.short('o')
				.long("only")
				.value_name("ONLY")
				.help("the pattern of files to exclusively show in the output")
				.value_parser(parse_regex),
		)
		.next_help_heading("Sorting")
		.arg(
			Arg::new("sort_bases")
				.short('s')
				.long("sort")
				.value_name("SORT_BASES")
				.help("the set of fields to sort by, trailing `_` reverses the direction")
				.action(ArgAction::Append)
				.default_values(["cat", "cname"])
				.value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(names(SortField::CLI_VALUES))),
		)

fn get_bool(matches: &clap::ArgMatches, name: &str) -> bool {
	matches
		.get_one::<String>(name)
		.map(|v| v == "true")
		.unwrap_or(false)
}

/// Parse the command line arguments, exiting on error or when help/version
/// was requested.
pub fn parse() -> Args {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare the original and the reimplementation on given args, in pty and pipe mode."""
import sys, os, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/tools")
from run import run, show

def pipe_run(exe, args, cwd, env=None):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, env=e)
    return p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace") + ("[stderr]" + p.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace") if p.stderr else "") + f"[exit {p.returncode}]"

def compare(args, cwd=".", cols=80, env=None, mode="both"):
    ok = True
    mine = "/workspace/target/release/pls"
    orig = "/workspace/executable"
    if mode in ("both", "pty"):
        a = run([orig] + args, cwd=cwd, cols=cols, env=env)
        b = run([mine] + args, cwd=cwd, cols=cols, env=env)
        a = a.replace("executable", "pls"); b = b.replace("pls", "pls")
        if a != b:
            ok = False
            print(f"PTY DIFF for {args} in {cwd} cols={cols}")
            import difflib
            for l in difflib.unified_diff(show(a).split("\n"), show(b).split("\n"), "orig", "mine", lineterm="", n=1):
                print(l)
    if mode in ("both", "pipe"):
        a = pipe_run(orig, args, cwd, env)
        b = pipe_run(mine, args, cwd, env)
        a = a.replace("executable", "pls")
        if a != b:
            ok = False
            print(f"PIPE DIFF for {args} in {cwd}")
            import difflib
            for l in difflib.unified_diff(show(a).split("\n"), show(b).split("\n"), "orig", "mine", lineterm="", n=1):
                print(l)
    return ok

if __name__ == "__main__":
    cwd = "."
    cols = 80
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if args and args[0].startswith("--cwd="):
        cwd = args[0][6:]; args = args[1:]
    if args and args[0].startswith("--cols="):
        cols = int(args[0][7:]); args = args[1:]
    if compare(args, cwd, cols):
        print("SAME")
EOF

//! Fork of `textwrap` crate
//!
//! Benefits of forking:
//! - Pull in only what we need rather than relying on the compiler to remove what we don't need
//! - `LineWrapper` is able to incrementally wrap which will help with `StyledStr`

pub(crate) mod core;
#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
pub(crate) mod word_separators;
#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
pub(crate) mod wrap_algorithms;

#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
pub(crate) fn wrap(content: &str, hard_width: usize) -> String {
    let mut wrapper = wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
    let mut total = Vec::new();
    for line in content.split_inclusive('\n') {
        wrapper.reset();
        let line = word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        total.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
    }
    total.join("")
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "wrap_help"))]
pub(crate) fn wrap(content: &str, _hard_width: usize) -> String {
    content.to_owned()
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct LineWrapper<'w> {
    hard_width: usize,
    line_width: usize,
    indentation: Option<&'w str>,
}

impl<'w> LineWrapper<'w> {
    pub(crate) fn new(hard_width: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            hard_width,
            line_width: 0,
            indentation: None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn reset(&mut self) {
        self.line_width = 0;
        self.indentation = None;
    }

    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, mut words: Vec<&'w str>) -> Vec<&'w str> {
        let mut first_word = false;
        if self.indentation.is_none() {
            first_word = true;
            if let Some(word) = words.first() {
                if word.trim().is_empty() {
                    self.indentation = Some(*word);
                } else {
                    self.indentation = Some("");
                }
            }
        }

        let mut i = 0;
        while i < words.len() {
            let word = &words[i];
            let trimmed = word.trim_end();
            let word_width = display_width(trimmed);
            let trimmed_delta = word.len() - trimmed.len();
            if first_word && 0 < word_width {
                // Never try to wrap the first word
                first_word = false;
            } else if self.hard_width < self.line_width + word_width {
                if 0 < i {
                    let prev = i - 1;
                    let trimmed = words[prev].trim_end();
                    words[prev] = trimmed;
                }

                self.line_width = 0;
                words.insert(i, "\n");
                i += 1;
                if let Some(indentation) = self.indentation {
                    words.insert(i, indentation);
                    self.line_width += indentation.len();
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            self.line_width += word_width + trimmed_delta;

            i += 1;
        }
        words
    }
}

pub(crate) fn find_words_ascii_space(line: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'_ str> + '_ {
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut in_whitespace = false;
    let mut char_indices = line.char_indices();

    std::iter::from_fn(move || {
        for (idx, ch) in char_indices.by_ref() {
            let next_whitespace = ch == ' ';
            if in_whitespace && !next_whitespace {
                let word = &line[start..idx];
                start = idx;
                in_whitespace = next_whitespace;
                return Some(word);
            }

            in_whitespace = next_whitespace;
        }

        if start < line.len() {
            let word = &line[start..];
            start = line.len();
            return Some(word);
        }

        None
    })
}

//! Terminal related helpers.

use std::mem::MaybeUninit;

/// Get the width of the terminal attached to the given file descriptor.
fn width_of(fd: libc::c_int) -> Option<usize> {
	unsafe {
		if libc::isatty(fd) != 1 {
			return None;
		}
		let mut ws = MaybeUninit::<libc::winsize>::zeroed();
		if libc::ioctl(fd, libc::TIOCGWINSZ, ws.as_mut_ptr()) == -1 {
			return None;
		}
		let ws = ws.assume_init();
		if ws.ws_col == 0 {
			None
		} else {
			Some(ws.ws_col as usize)
		}
	}
}

/// Get the width of the terminal connected to standard output, if any.
pub fn stdout_width() -> Option<usize> {

//! A node is a single file system entry along with everything needed to
//! display it.

use std::fs::Metadata;
use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::time::SystemTime;

use crate::args::Args;
use crate::config::Conf;
use crate::enums::{Collapse, DetailField, Typ};
use crate::fmt::{wrap, Style};
use crate::models::owner;
use crate::models::symlink::SymTarget;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Node {
	/// The name shown in the output.
	pub name: String,
	/// The full path to the node.
	pub path: PathBuf,
	/// Metadata obtained without following symlinks.
	pub meta: Metadata,
	pub typ: Typ,
	pub conf: Rc<Conf>,
	/// Style directives contributed by the matching specs.
	pub spec_style: String,
	pub importance: i8,
	/// The glyph to show before the name, if any.
	pub icon: Option<String>,
	pub collapse: Option<Collapse>,
	/// Whether the node was given on the command line (as opposed to being
	/// read from a directory).
	pub is_arg: bool,
	pub children: Vec<Node>,
}

impl Node {
	/// Create a node for an entry inside a directory.
	pub fn new(name: String, path: PathBuf, meta: Metadata, conf: Rc<Conf>, is_arg: bool) -> Self {
		let typ = Typ::from_file_type(&meta.file_type());
		let match_name = path
			.file_name()
			.map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
			.unwrap_or_else(|| name.clone());
		let mut node = Self {
			name,
			path,
			meta,
			typ,
			conf,
			spec_style: String::new(),
			importance: 0,
			icon: None,
			collapse: None,
			is_arg,
			children: vec![],
		};
		node.apply_specs(&match_name);
